scenes.title: Recover the original assumption
scenes.visual: Editable assumption ID and original-rule cards
scenes.narration: Start with the original assumption, customer context and before-test review rule. Preserve the wording and source history. Do not rewrite an assumption after a test and claim the new wording was always tested.

scenes.title: Check source status and fit
scenes.narration: Use your experiment log and customer evidence review. Actual, planned and rehearsal sources have different status. Ask whether each source addresses this exact claim. A clarity check cannot establish payment.

scenes.title: Compare support and challenge
scenes.narration: Record both supporting and challenging information, with context and source quality. Preserve contradictions, deviations, assistance and missingness. Do not select only the evidence that confirms your first belief.

scenes.title: Assess within scope
scenes.visual: Supported within scope / Weakened / Mixed / Unknown cards
scenes.narration: Choose a reasoned assessment. Supported within scope means relevant evidence supports a narrow claim. Weakened means it challenges the assumption. Mixed means sources differ. Unknown means evidence is absent or insufficient.

scenes.title: Keep uncertainty visible
scenes.narration: If only fictional rehearsal or planned tests exist, actual customer evidence remains unknown. Even a supported narrow claim leaves other assumptions unresolved, including adoption, payment, retention and feasibility. Avoid invented confidence scores.

scenes.title: Write the comparison
scenes.narration: Create your Assumption Evidence Comparison with original claim, sources, evidence fit, support, challenge, assessment and next action. This begins the decision module; it does not approve launch, funding or market demand.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Compare the claim with evidence that actually fits.

children: An
assumption
is a belief that needs checking.
Evidence fit
asks whether the source addresses that exact claim. An
assessment
summarises the comparison within its scope, with reasons and limits.
Recover the original assumption, context and before-test rule.
Reference the experiment log and customer evidence review manually.
Check source status, quality and fit to this exact claim.
Record support and challenge, including contradictory or missing records.
Choose a reasoned assessment and show what changed.
Keep unresolved assumptions visible and plan the next learning action.
Four assessment choices
Supported within scope:
relevant evidence supports a narrow claim.
Weakened:
relevant evidence challenges it.
Mixed:
sources differ.
Unknown:
evidence is absent or insufficient.
Evidence must fit
An uncoached explanation can inform clarity. A task action can inform a bounded behaviour claim. Neither automatically tests actual payment, repeat usage or feasible delivery.
Illustrative comparison — no real results

A01: relevant adults understand a registration concept without coaching. E01 is planned/not run; R01 is fictional rehearsal. Actual customer evidence: none. Assessment: unknown. Next action: resolve access/safeguards and run an appropriately permitted clarity check. Payment and adoption remain separate unknowns.

If a future actual clarity test supports A01, report the context and source limits; do not change the conclusion to “customers will buy.” If sources disagree, preserve that disagreement. Record revisions as new wording with a change reason rather than rewriting the original history.

No numerical confidence or demand score is generated. Field presence is not evidence quality. Use anonymous summaries here, with private originals in approved secure storage. No source verification, experiment or human approval is connected.
